newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadians resigned to prolonged jobless crisis.
newsitem.headline: Canadians resigned to prolonged jobless crisis.

text.p: Elected more than three years ago on a "jobs, jobs, jobs" platform, Canada's Liberal government can claim only partial success on this key economic front.
More than 300,000 new jobs were created in 1996, but Canada's unemployment rate continues to hover at the 10 percent level.

This week's federal budget contained no new strategy to fight joblessness. Instead, Canadian Finance Minister Paul Martin hopes the government's strategy of reducing the budget deficit and encouraging economic growth will produce a jobs windfall.
The most Martin would promise was C$30 million (US$22 million) to improve the job prospects of the disabled and pension adjustments to make it easier for Canadians to change employers.

"Those modest initiatives aren't surprising because government is trying to get out of the business of job creation and into the business of promoting healthy economic fundamentals," said Rob Palombi, economist with MMS International.
Despite pockets of outrage, Canadians remain resigned to the bleak employment picture.
Palombi expects a mood swing if Canadians do not see some sort of economic payoff in the next couple of years.
